# Question

These are simulated teaching data from 24 independently potted seedlings,
randomly assigned to control or nutrient treatment. Length was measured at the
start and after seven days. What does growth look like in the two groups?

Replace or extend this paragraph as you work through the course.

# Data and methods

The plant/pot is the independent experimental unit. Length and growth are in
millimetres. Growth is final length minus initial length. The raw input is kept
in `data/seedlings.csv` and is not edited by this report.

```{r import}
seedlings <- read_csv("data/seedlings.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
seedlings <- seedlings |>
  mutate(growth_mm = final_mm - initial_mm)
nrow(seedlings)
```

# Results

There are `r nrow(seedlings)` plants in the input table.

```{r group-summary}
group_summary <- seedlings |>
  group_by(treatment) |>
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    mean_growth_mm = mean(growth_mm),
    sd_growth_mm = sd(growth_mm),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
knitr::kable(group_summary, digits = 2,
             caption = "Growth summaries. SD describes variation among plants.")
```

```{r growth-plot, fig.cap="Seven-day growth of individual seedlings. Points are individual plants; horizontal displacement only separates overlapping points."}
ggplot(seedlings, aes(x = treatment, y = growth_mm)) +
  geom_point(position = position_jitter(width = 0.08, height = 0, seed = 7)) +
  labs(x = "Nutrient allocation", y = "Growth over seven days (mm)") +
  theme_minimal()
```

# Interpretation

Write two or three sentences about the direction of the observed difference,
variation among plants, and what these simulated observations do and do not
establish. The template deliberately leaves this interpretation for you.
